subject.title: [codex] Verify Telegram topic proof for cron delivery

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose validateDeliveryResults as a plugin SDK hook and intentionally fail non-General Telegram topic delivery after Telegram may already have sent the message when provider topic proof is missing or mismatched?
rationale: Both the API expansion and the fail-closed retry semantics are compatibility-sensitive product contracts; code correctness and green tests cannot determine whether maintainers want external plugins and users to rely on them.

options.title: Adopt the generic contract
options.body: Keep the documented optional hook and fail-closed Telegram validator, with sent-before-error behavior treated as the canonical retry-safety contract.

options.title: Keep validation Telegram-local
options.body: Remove the public SDK hook and perform this proof check inside the Telegram-owned cron/outbound integration to avoid establishing a general plugin contract.

options.title: Preserve current behavior
options.body: Decline post-send fail-closed validation if the risk of false failures and duplicate retries outweighs stronger topic attestation.

recommendation.title: Adopt the generic contract
recommendation.body: Keep the documented optional hook and fail-closed Telegram validator, with sent-before-error behavior treated as the canonical retry-safety contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history shows the strongest ownership of both the plugin SDK boundary and core outbound delivery lifecycle.
